what_happened: A docs job to design a warm baseline build, meant to cut the time of the checks stage, was rejected at final verification. The verifier raised one major finding. The design document (docs/design/warm-baseline-build.md) leaves out the CI-result path that the checks stage already uses. So for most jobs the design would not shorten the stage it targets. The sections named are Problem, Why this removes the bottleneck, and Alternatives considered. No acceptance criterion is listed as unmet and no check is listed as failed.
cause: The design was written without surveying how the checks stage works today. It did not establish that most jobs already take their check results from CI. Nothing at the reading or planning stage requires a design doc to describe the current mechanism, or to show measured stage time for the case it targets, before it proposes a replacement. The "why this removes the bottleneck" claim was therefore never tested against the real flow. The only comparison with the existing code and path was the verifier's, after the spend.
prevention: Add a required "current state" step to design-doc jobs. Before proposing a mechanism, the planner or producer must list the existing code paths and results that already serve the capability. For a speed design, it must also give measured stage durations split by path (CI-result reuse vs. local run). The critic then rejects a design whose bottleneck claim does not cover each existing path, and the doc must say what share of jobs the change affects.
proposed_request: Revise docs/design/warm-baseline-build.md, the design for a warm baseline build to cut checks-stage time, so it accounts for the CI-result path the checks stage already uses. Outcome: the Problem section describes how the checks stage gets its results today, including when it reuses a CI result and when it runs checks locally. It gives measured durations for each path from recorded past jobs, with the source of each number. The doc states what share of jobs still run checks locally and so would benefit from a warm baseline. The "Why this removes the bottleneck" section is based on those numbers, and the "Alternatives considered" section includes extending or improving CI-result reuse as an alternative, with a reasoned comparison. If the warm baseline would not shorten the stage for most jobs, the doc says so and gives a recommendation. Only the design doc and its changelog entry change. No code or config is changed.
